_doc: Anti-drift compass for the PM SCHEDULER DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-28: 'let's now plan for another page' -> PM Scheduler, chosen after measuring the candidates). Companion to PM_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/pm_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per PMK class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new PMK dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the screens, handlers, tables and derived values the journey touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B at spoke 5; retrieve-first, crawl on a genuine bag miss
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

PM01.notes: First run - a hive with registered assets but no PM program yet. The empty/first-run state was never mapped by the PDDA arc.

PM02.notes: Register a PM asset -> scope items -> frequency. G: the PDDA arc mapped the 3-screen wizard (screen-dashboard / screen-add / screen-detail), saveAsset/saveNewTask, and the canonical FREQ registry + canonFreq().

PM03.notes: The triage dashboard. G: the PDDA arc fixed worst-first sort (overdue was buried on page 2, now position 0) and getAssetOverallStatus. Per-ROLE triage is unwalked - a tech and a supervisor want different orderings.

PM04.notes: Complete a PM at the asset (checklist, readings, sign-off). G: pmCompleteHandler + markDone mapped; the completion writes pm_completions and mirrors to logbook.

PM05.notes: PRIORITY. Complete -> next_due_date recompute -> the card changes state. G partial: the PDDA arc verified ONE reschedule loop live (overdue Weekly -> complete -> next_due +7), but the recompute is DERIVED in v_pm_scope_items_truth and its completeness across frequency bands and personas is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ARITHMETIC IS CLEAN: next_due_date is DERIVED in v_pm_scope_items_truth from COALESCE(last_completed_at, anchor_date, created_at) + frequency_days, and every consumer reads the derived columns rather than recomputing - alert-hub, dayplanner, hive and logbook all select is_overdue / days_until_due / next_due_date straight from the view, and hive.html documents deleting its own HIVE_FREQ_DAYS map on 2026-05-20 for exactly this reason. So a completion re-derives everywhere by construction, and PMK4 now pins the frequency_days half of that derivation against the client. Recorded as a real clean result. THE DEFECT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE TRANSITION - WHETHER THE READER IS TOLD WHAT THEY ARE LOOKING AT. analytics.html renders analytics_snapshots: the first view of the PHT day computes and saves, every later view replays the saved copy, and only Refresh recomputes. Good feature. But the source chip hardcoded 'Live recomputation each refresh' on EVERY load. Measured: the KPI numbers were on screen at 0ms, up to ~24h old, under a chip promising they were live. In this journey's terms: a tech completes a PM, opens analytics, compliance has not moved, and nothing says the number predates their work. FIXED: the chip now reports which of the two it actually is, per phase (one tab can be a snapshot while another was just recomputed) - 'Saved snapshot, computed 1 min ago - Refresh to recompute' vs 'Recomputed just now', verified live in both states and both languages. Three call sites had to be reconciled, because the chip is first drawn BEFORE hydration decides snapshot-vs-live: the live fetch, the post-hydration render, and the phase switch. My first attempt fixed only the live path and the cached load kept the false claim - the same two-render-paths mistake PMK1 caught, made twice in one arc. GATED by tools/validate_source_chip_freshness.py (registered): a page reading a *_snapshots/*_cache table must COMPUTE its freshness string, never hardcode a liveness claim. The existing 'Source-chip truth' dimension only checks that a chip names views the page READS, which is how this shipped green. Teeth proven by restoring the hardcoded claim: exit 1.

PM06.notes: Completion -> logbook mirror (pm_completion_id lineage). G: gate #27 pm_mirror_asset_lineage locks the CREATE lineage, and the logbook arc seeded 40 mirrored completions so the journey is finally demonstrable (it was 0/1591 before).

PM07.notes: THE KEYSTONE. MEASURED 2026-07-28 before this roadmap existed: across 1,224 consecutive-completion intervals, 331 (27.0%) were completed AFTER frequency_days had elapsed, and 14.5% at more than 1.5x the interval - while get_pm_compliance_smrp reports 85.7-87.5% per hive, which reads as near-world-class against the 90% benchmark. The RPC counts a completion whenever it lands in the period, regardless of whether it was on schedule. HARVESTED (bag miss -> crawl): the SMRP-derived standard states PM compliance = completed / scheduled x 100, world-class 90%, and explicitly that it 'does not account for late PMs' (substrate/external/external-pm-schedule-compliance-metric.md). W/R open: the walk needs 2 personas x 2 states, and the disposition (surface on-time% beside compliance% vs change the metric) is a judgement to make WITH the walk, not before it. WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28, TWO personas in TWO hives, and the contradiction is on the glass: supervisor/Lucena sees '0 of 31 on track now - 88% PM compliance (SMRP)' with 20 overdue, and worker/Manila sees '3 of 30 on track now - 86% PM compliance (SMRP)' with 24 overdue. The page's headline ('PM compliance is in the red') and its next-action ('Assign 24 overdue PMs') are honest; the SMRP figure sits in the ON TRACK card's subtitle right beside the real-time count, so a historical late-blind metric reads as reassurance about the present. QUANTIFIED by the new detector: compliance 86.3% vs on-time 73.0% = a 13.3-POINT flattery. R PARTIAL and deliberately so: the gap is now MEASURED and ratcheted (tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py, registered, teeth proven), but SURFACING an on-time figure beside the compliance figure is a product change to a number a plant acts on - that is the next unit, not a drive-by. CLOSED 2026-07-28. The measure existed only inside a validator's SQL, so the page still showed only the flattering half. Built get_pm_ontime_delivery (migration 20260728000005) as the ONE definition - hive-scoped, period-aware, membership-gated the same way as get_pm_compliance_smrp (both a foreign hive and a NULL platform-wide read from an authenticated caller are rejected 42501, probed). get_pm_compliance_smrp is deliberately UNCHANGED: it implements a named standard and holds verified parity with analytics. SURFACED on the PM Scheduler card as '72.5% done on time - 123 of 447 ran late' beside the 88%, with the late COUNT named because that is the form a supervisor can act on. Walked in both hives: Lucena 88/72.5, Manila 86/74.7, each matching the DB exactly. THE FULL-PAGE VIEW FOUND WHAT THE CARD DID NOT: the page said 'PM compliance is in the red - 29 assets are overdue' in its banner and 'STAIR-READY' on this card at 0 of 31 on track, because the tag read compliance alone and 88 >= 80. The ladder now runs on the WEAKER of compliance and on-time - same 80/60 thresholds, no invented standard, on the principle that a program is only as ready as its weakest measure. Safe because the canonical maturity Stair is a composite from compute_hive_readiness (canonical/standards.json), which this local heuristic only ever approximated; the analytics arc had already grepped that overall_pct is not consumed by hive_readiness. Lucena now reads BUILDING/amber and no longer contradicts its own banner. CLS: the new line reserves the two lines it fills (measured 31px at 390px and desktop), so it costs zero shift.

PM08.notes: Change an asset's frequency -> the whole schedule re-derives. G partial: the frequency VOCABULARY is canonical and gated (canonFreq + freq_crosspage_consistent), and asset-hub's RCM interval writer was fixed - but a frequency CHANGE on an existing program, and whether every derived surface re-derives, is unwalked. WALKED 2026-07-28 and the defect is upstream of the change itself. A PM's frequency is a WORD in the DB, and the schedule is DERIVED from that word by a CASE in v_pm_scope_items_truth - so every writer that turns an interval in DAYS into that word is deciding the real schedule, and TWO of them did it differently. integrations.html (the CMMS/CSV import a plant uses to onboard its EXISTING program) had a local map with NO Daily bucket, taking the first bucket >= days over [7,30,90,180,365]: measured, 1 day -> 'Weekly' (7x rarer than the source system asked), 14 -> 'Monthly' (2.1x), 45 -> 'Quarterly' (2x). Every drift ran the SAME direction, less often than specified - the direction that leaves equipment un-inspected. asset-hub.html rounded to the NEAREST bucket instead, so a 300-day RCM interval became 'Annual' (365). FIXED with ONE shared mapping (whFreqFromDays / whFreqDays in utils.js, loaded platform-wide) that snaps DOWN to the closest bucket not exceeding the requested interval: rounding to a shorter interval costs labour, rounding to a longer one is a safety decision. Verified live on integrations.html: 1/2/3d now Daily, 14d Weekly, 45d Monthly, 300d Semi-Annual, and zero intervals in 1..400 remain rarer than asked. The only floor is sub-daily (0.5d -> Daily), which the six-label vocabulary genuinely cannot express. ALSO PINNED, LATENT: the UI's canonFreq resolves 'biweekly'/'fortnightly' to Weekly (7d) while the view says 14d - so such a row would show a Weekly badge on a fortnightly schedule. No such rows exist (all 416 scope items map cleanly: weekly 102, monthly 99, quarterly 93, annual 91, semi-annual 31), making this the logbook arc's LG2 shape - agreement by luck of vocabulary - so the gate asserts it rather than waiting for the first import that uses the word. The view's ELSE 30 catch-all is the same bomb: 'Every 500 hours' displays as the UI's 'Other' bucket while the DB silently schedules it monthly. GATED by tools/validate_pm_frequency_mapping.py (parity live vs utils.js, safe-direction over 1..400, and no page carrying a private bucket list), registered in run_platform_checks; teeth proven by restoring the private map (exit 1) and reverting (exit 0).

PM09.notes: Skip / defer a PM. pm_completions carries status='skipped' (~5% of seeded rows) but nothing models what a skip MEANS in the compliance number - neither silently compliant nor silently overdue. Feeds PMK5. WALKED 2026-07-28. THE ANSWER TO THE JOURNEY'S QUESTION IS YES - the numbers are honest, and that is a real result, not an absence of one. Proven in a rolled-back transaction: inserting a status='skipped' completion moved neither the hive's compliance (85.7 -> 85.7) nor the scope item's next_due_date. A skip therefore cannot be used to clear an overdue flag or flatter the program. That honesty rests on three independent status='done' filters (the compliance RPC, the on-time RPC, and the truth view's last_completed_at LATERAL), any one of which a later edit could drop, so it is now asserted rather than left to luck - teeth proven by replacing the on-time RPC with one that omits the filter (exit 1). AN INSTRUMENT ERROR OF MY OWN, caught before it became a false finding: grepping the pages for the literal 'skipped' returned nothing outside backup dirs, and I nearly recorded 'no surface shows a skip'. The detail view DOES render them - it tests c.status === 'done' ? 'Completed' : 'Deferred', so it matches on the COMPLEMENT and my literal grep could never have found it. THE REAL GAP IS REACHABILITY, recorded honestly rather than papered over: 78 skipped rows exist and render as 'Deferred' in the per-asset history, but NOTHING in the page can create one. A technician who cannot do a PM has no way to say so - the choice is to leave it overdue (indistinguishable from untouched) or mark it done, which is a lie. Building that flow is a product decision, not a defect fix, so it is written here rather than invented mid-arc. The related triage gap: the dashboard cannot distinguish overdue-and-untouched from deferred-with-a-reason. FIXTURE FIXED (the seeder decides what can be tested - HK2's lesson again): status and note were drawn INDEPENDENTLY, so 'skipped' rows carried completion notes - 78 skips saying things like 'All readings nominal', which is incoherent, since if the readings were nominal the PM was done. Status and note are now generated together (_completion_status_and_note) with real skip reasons - 'Line still running, could not isolate', 'Deferred: no spare gasket in stores'. Verified over 400 draws: 29 skips, 0 incoherent.

PM10.notes: Compliance rollup parity across page / analytics / hive PM Health / shift-brain. G: the PDDA arc verified SMRP 87.1% single-RPC parity between page and analytics. The other two consumers, and parity under a CHANGED program, are unwalked.

PM11.notes: PRIORITY. Amend or delete a completion after sign-off. O partial on MEASURED evidence from the logbook arc's LG4 sweep: pm_completions has 6 user triggers and NONE of them audit, so an amendment by any path that skips the page leaves no record - exactly the weakness LG4 closed for logbook with trg_logbook_post_close_audit. HARVEST: that arc's own finding plus the pattern and migration to copy (20260728000003). Feeds PMK3. WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28 and the defect is the sharp version. A technician silently BACK-DATED their own completion by 400 days: one row affected, no error, nothing recorded anywhere. completed_at is the most consequential field on a compliance record - it drives the compliance window, the on-time measure and next_due_date - so moving it moves the number a plant and an auditor both read: back-dating a late PM makes it on-time. Unlike logbook, there was no client-written audit row either, so the trigger is not a backstop here, it is the ONLY record there has ever been. FIXED by migration 20260728000004: an AFTER UPDATE trigger recording amend_pm_completion with completed_at before/after, status before/after, and days_moved - the number an auditor actually wants. Scoped to fields that change what the record CLAIMS (completed_at / status / scope_item_id), so a notes edit stays silent and the log remains readable enough to be audited. Proven in a rolled-back transaction: insert 0 rows, notes-edit 0 rows, back-date 1 row with days_moved -400.00. The probe row was restored exactly. GATED by extending tools/validate_pm_write_isolation.py (the arc's own gate template) from 4 checks to 5; teeth proven by dropping the trigger (exit 1) and re-applying (exit 0).

PM12.notes: Delete a PM asset -> what happens to its scope items, its completion history and the compliance denominator. The 2 unconfirmed DB writes (pm_assets update + delete, ~L2640) live here. Feeds PMK6. WALKED 2026-07-28 and it is the most consequential defect of the arc so far. pm_completions.asset_id and pm_scope_items.asset_id both CASCADE from pm_assets, so deleting one asset destroys its whole compliance history. Probed live in a rolled-back transaction as a WORKER: deleting 'Caterpillar 3516B' took 31 completion records and 8 scope items, history reaching back to 2026-04-29, and left ZERO audit rows at the database. Those 31 rows are the evidence that named people did named jobs on dated occasions; they feed compliance %, on-time delivery and the reliability figures downstream, so the deletion also rewrites HISTORICAL compliance. TWO SEPARATE HOLES. (1) AUTHORIZATION: pm-scheduler gates the Delete button to a supervisor or the asset's author and even toasts 'Only supervisors can delete other members' assets' - but that rule lived ONLY in the page. pm_assets_write is a single ALL policy satisfied by ANY active member, so a worker writing through the db client deleted a supervisor's asset. The canonical UI-only-gate-is-bypassable class, with the sharpest possible payload. (2) EVIDENCE: there was no DELETE trigger on pm_assets at all; the only record was one the PAGE wrote afterwards, which any non-page write skips - and which never knew what the cascade cost. FIXED by migration 20260728000006: a RESTRICTIVE DELETE policy (ANDed with the existing permissive one, the smallest change that cannot widen anything else) matching the rule the UI already states, plus a BEFORE DELETE trigger that counts the children while they still exist and records completions_destroyed / scope_items_destroyed / history_began. Proven: WORKER delete -> 0 rows, SUPERVISOR delete -> 1 row, audit meta reads {completions_destroyed: 31, scope_items_destroyed: 8, history_began: 2026-04-29}. THE CLIENT ALSO CLAIMED A REFUSED DELETE AS DONE: deleteAsset() tested only `if (error)`, and a PostgREST delete matching nothing returns error:null - so it toasted success, wrote an audit row for a deletion that never happened, and dropped the asset locally so it silently returned on reload. The restrictive policy makes that path REACHABLE rather than theoretical, so it is now confirmed with .select('id'); the client-side audit write was deleted outright because the trigger supersedes it and duplicating it would double-count. GATED: validate_pm_write_isolation grew from 5 checks to 8 (delete_role_gated live-probes a worker deleting an asset they did not author; delete_audited and delete_policy_present assert the trigger and policy survive a later migration). Teeth proven by dropping the policy: 2 checks fail, exit 1.

PM13.notes: Cross-hive boundary: a foreign completion must not inflate another hive's compliance. G: ALREADY HARDENED by the PDDA arc - 3 write holes fixed by migration 20260712000012, gate validate_pm_write_isolation.py 4/4, and get_pm_compliance_smrp raises 42501 for a non-member. The walk re-confirms it from the UI side across personas rather than re-litigating it.

PM14.notes: Parts / readings on a PM. G: the PDDA arc's reuse verdict was completion->logbook = the canonical FUSION (one event) and parts-on-a-PM = KEEP-DISTINCT (logbook owns parts). The walk tests whether that boundary holds for a tech who consumed parts during a PM.

PM15.notes: Mobile 390px at-the-asset completion - the tech is THE persona for this page. G partial: the PDDA arc's A-axis was axe-clean (0 violations) but axe measures a11y, not one-handed reachability of the completion flow.

PM16.notes: Templates + scope-item reuse across assets. G partial: populateTemplateOptions / selectTmplCat / pickTaskChip mapped; whether a template edit propagates to assets already using it is unwalked.

PM17.notes: Shift-brain 'PMs Due' + the AI companion grounding must read the same truth as the page. G partial: setPmCompanionContext ships a piiSafe snapshot (registered live by the PDDA arc); the shift-planner-orchestrator's PM read is a separate path and unverified against the page.

PM18.notes: Offline completion at the asset - the plant has no signal where the machine is. pm-scheduler registers a shared queue (window._whPmQueue via whCreateQueue, table pm_completions), which the logbook arc's LG3 fix now protects from reporting a lost write as synced. The journey itself is unwalked.

PMK1.name: On-time is not the same as done
PMK1.notes: OPEN on measured evidence. RULE: a compliance metric must distinguish a PM completed ON SCHEDULE from one completed late, or it flatters the program to the person least able to check it. EVIDENCE (2026-07-28): 331 of 1,224 intervals (27.0%) ran past frequency_days, 14.5% past 1.5x, while the RPC reports 85.7-87.5%. HARVEST: crawled on a genuine bag miss - the corpus held 144 external chunks and NOT ONE on maintenance; substrate/external/external-pm-schedule-compliance-metric.md now states the formula, the 90% world-class benchmark, and the explicit blind spot ('does not account for late PMs'). DETECT/FIX/GATE open: the disposition is a real judgement (surface an on-time% beside compliance%, vs change what compliance means) and belongs WITH the walk, since changing a number a plant acts on is not a drive-by. DETECT DONE: tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py computes both figures like-for-like (it mirrors the RPC's own scheduled-count so the comparison is fair) and holds the GAP as a forward-only ratchet at 13.3 points. SWEEP DONE: the metric has exactly one producer - get_pm_compliance_smrp - which every consumer (page, analytics, hive PM Health, shift-brain) reads, so there is no second definition to reconcile; the class is about what that one definition CANNOT SEE, not about drift between definitions. FIX/GATE remain open: the gate exists but the product still shows only the flattering number, and deciding whether to surface on-time% beside it, or to change what compliance means, is a judgement for Ian since it moves a figure a plant acts on and is covered by a named standard. SWEEP DONE - and the sibling held the SHARPER version of the defect. analytics.html labelled the SMRP completed/scheduled counts '541 of 618 PMs on time'. Those counts say nothing about lateness; the standard explicitly does not account for late PMs, and 27.0% of 1,224 intervals ran past their own frequency. The words 'on time' claimed the one thing the number cannot support, in both EN and FIL ('nasa oras'). Relabelled to 'PMs completed' / 'natapos', and the real figure added from the same RPC. Two stale code comments quoting the old label (descriptive.py, validate_pm_compliance_weighted.py) were corrected in the same change. TWO MORE FOUND IN THE SAME CARD: (1) its ladder used 'LOW', the ambiguous string that was fixed to 'BELOW STAIR' on the PM card in the 2026-05-14 walkthrough and never swept here; (2) the label and footnote both read '30 days' STATICALLY while the page defaults to 90 and never rewrote them on a period switch - so a 90-day number was labelled 30 days in both languages. Both now written from the payload's own period_days, verified across a FIL round-trip and a live 30<->90 switch. A TIMING BUG OF MY OWN, caught by verifying rather than assuming: the summary renders from TWO paths and the cached one (loadSnapshots) paints without ever calling fetchPhase, so the first version of this fix silently never showed the figure on the common load. Fixed by firing on both paths and repainting when the RPC lands.
PMK1.gate: tools/validate_pm_ontime_vs_compliance.py (gap ratchet + RPC/inline parity, per hive)

PMK2.name: A derived schedule needs a real denominator
PMK2.notes: OPEN on measured evidence, and deliberately framed as LATENT-AND-CONTAINED rather than 'compliance is wrong'. get_pm_compliance_smrp charges GREATEST(1, period/frequency_days) scheduled events, so in a 90-day window a Semi-annual PM (31 items) counts as 1 when it is truly due 0.5 times and an Annual PM (91 items) counts as 1 against a true 0.25 - 122 of 416 scope items (29%) structurally over-counted. MEASURED IMPACT TODAY: under one point per hive (85.7->85.3, 85.7->86.1, 87.5->87.1), because those items happen to carry completions in the window. So the honest disposition is the LG2 one: allow the approximation, make divergence detectable, and let a gate catch the day the data stops being kind. Same source as PMK1.

PMK3.name: Completion immutability is tamper-EVIDENT at the database
PMK3.notes: EARNED BY THE PM11 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: for a record that drives a regulated number, 'tamper-evident' has to mean the DATABASE recorded the amendment - a client-written row is skipped by any write that does not go through the page, and here there was no client-written row at all. EVIDENCE: a completion back-dated 400 days, silently, by its own author (pm_completions RLS is owner-scoped write, so this is a legitimate author doing an illegitimate thing). HARVEST: the logbook arc's LG4, whose migration and scoping decision transferred directly. FIX + GATE as recorded on PM11. SWEEP PARTIAL: inventory_items carries the same client-only-audit weakness (measured in the logbook arc's LG4 sweep, still unfixed) and pm_assets/pm_scope_items have not been checked for whether their amendments matter the same way. SWEEP COMPLETED BY PM12: tamper-evidence has to cover DESTRUCTION, not just amendment. A completion cannot be silently edited any more, but until 20260728000006 the entire history could be removed by deleting its parent asset - a bigger hole reached by a different door, and open to any member rather than the record's author. The general rule: for a record that drives a regulated number, enumerate every path that can CHANGE OR REMOVE it (direct update, parent cascade, bulk delete) and make each one leave a database-level trace. The trigger must run BEFORE the cascade, or the thing worth recording - how much was destroyed - is already gone.

PMK4.name: The word that sets the schedule must mean the same thing to every writer
PMK4.notes: EARNED BY THE PM08 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: when a schedule is DERIVED from a stored label, the label-producing code IS the scheduler. Any page converting a duration into that label must use ONE shared mapping whose day-values equal the deriving view's, and must round toward MORE frequent - under-scheduling a PM is a safety decision, over-scheduling is a cost one. EVIDENCE: two writers, two rules, neither matching the view; the CMMS import silently made every sub-weekly PM weekly. DISTINCT FROM PMK1 (which is about a metric flattering what was DONE) - this is about the SCHEDULE ITSELF being quietly wrong before any work happens. SWEEP: both known writers fixed; the gate fails any third page that grows its own bucket list.
